equityFacts: [FACT — Hero equity vs the modeled villain range(s), computed on-device by Monte Carlo (10000 trials), NOT by you: pre-flop ~34%, flop ~44%, turn ~40%, river ~39%. A low number means hero loses to most of villain's range and is at best a weak bluff-catcher.]

[FACT — Villain MrWhite (CO) range behind the equity above: Pre-flop: 3-bet vs a middle-position open → 3-bet range (~6% of hands); Flop: bet (~75% pot) → polarized: top 30% value + bottom 16% bluffs; Turn: check → range unchanged; River: check → range unchanged.]

[HEURISTIC — Equity REALIZATION (raw equity discounted for hero's position + hand class; ESTIMATED, not exact): flop ~44% → realized ~33% (OOP, a marginal made hand); turn ~40% → realized ~45% (OOP, a strong made hand); river ~39% → realized ~44% (OOP, a strong made hand). A marginal hand out of position rarely realizes its raw equity; a strong made hand over-realizes. Weigh the continue / bluff-catch read against the REALIZED figure, not the raw one — but this is heuristic context: a decisive pot-odds price FACT and the hard equity FACT above still take precedence.]

[HEURISTIC — SPR & COMMITMENT (effective stack ÷ pot, hero-centric; ESTIMATED, not exact): flop SPR ~7.9 — to get all-in profitably needs ~47% equity (high SPR — favours pot control with one-pair hands); turn SPR ~2.9 — to get all-in profitably needs ~43% equity (low SPR — favours stacking off strong made hands); river SPR ~2.9 — to get all-in profitably needs ~43% equity (low SPR — favours stacking off strong made hands). Use this for the call-vs-raise / stack-off decision, NOT the bluff-catch call (pot odds govern that): at low SPR a strong-enough made hand should commit, at high SPR a one-pair hand favours pot control. With a marginal made hand villain's stack-off range skews to sets/two-pair, so require more than the raw %. The stack-off % is the equity to get all-in profitably versus a willing range, NOT hero's pot-odds price. This is heuristic context — a decisive pot-odds price FACT and the hard equity FACT still take precedence.]
